messages:
maya: Heads up — two prod GPU nodes scaled down at 12:34 and terminated long-running training pods. We lost checkpoint uploads for 3 jobs, started at ~00:00 UTC.

ton y: ugh. did CA/scale-down logs show why pods were evicted? any PDBs on those pods?

maya: cluster-autoscaler triggered scale-down. The pods had no PDBs and no cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict annotation. They were not daemonsets and were Requesting GPUs (nvidia.com/gpu).

kai: quick note: CA generally honours PDBs for voluntary disruptions. For non-evictable pods (local storage, GPUs, or no graceful eviction handler) CA should avoid downscaling nodes that would leave those pods orphaned. Which CA version are we on?

sre-oncall: 1.24.2 (deployed via helm chart stable/cluster-autoscaler). Logs: "scaleDown: node gpupool-3 eligible but pods not evictable" then a follow-up where drain command ran and kubelet killed containers.

ton y: could be our drain hook. If we use a custom drain script in cluster-autoscaler or node termination webhook that forces kubelet eviction, it can bypass PDBs if you pass force flags. Need to check.

maya: short-term mitigation ideas: add pod annotation cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false" for active training pods so CA won't consider them for eviction, and add a job-runner step to cordon nodes during large experiments.

kai: longer term: we should standardize three pieces: priorityClass for long-running GPU workloads, targeted PDBs for replica sets where we can tolerate one less replica, and a checkpoint-safe drain workflow that signals pods to checkpoint before eviction.

maya: example PDB + PriorityClass we can drop into our job template:
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: model-trainer-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: model-trainer
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: gpu-training
value: 800000
globalDefault: false
description: "High priority for long-running GPU training jobs"
```

ton y: operational note: PDBs with minAvailable can prevent any scale-down if applied too broadly. We should scope selectors to job-runner labels (e.g., job-group) and not blanket-match all trainers. Also prefer priorityClass over making everything non-evictable.

kai: additional operational controls:
- label gpu nodepool nodes with node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true and have CA scale-down logic prefer draining nodes only when replacement capacity exists
- implement node annotation node.alpha.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled set by job orchestration for scheduled runs
- set pod annotation cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=false during checkpoint windows

sre-oncall: can we add a safe-drain helper? flow: cordon -> trigger "checkpoint" signal to sidecar -> wait up to 10m for checkpoint to finish -> kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data (no --force) which will respect PDBs. If the pod does not checkpoint, fail and uncordon.

maya: agree. I'll add a sidecar spec in the examples and documentation. Also open PR to add a helm value to set the gpu training priorityClass and example PDB per-job.

ton y: I'll own the automation for node annotations: before a scheduled run the job-runner sets node annotation node.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true on all nodes in the pool, and removes it after completion. We should also have a fallback TTL so orphan annotations don't block forever.

infra-bot: deploy check: created branch gpu-scale-safety, CI passed (lint, unit tests).

maya: thanks all. Action items: tony - automation for node annotation + TTL; kai - add PriorityClass + scoped PDB helm templates; maya - sidecar & docs + PR for job templates; sre-oncall - add safe-drain runbook and verify CA flags (skip-nodes-with-local-storage / check versioning). I'll open tickets for each.

maya: one follow-up: let's audit other pools for pods that lack safe-to-evict annotation. If anyone finds jobs that silently assume eviction, flag them so we can update templates.

kai: noted. I'll run a k8s query tomorrow: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.spec.containers[0].resources.requests["nvidia.com/gpu"]) ]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {.metadata.annotations.cluster-autoscaler\.kubernetes\.io/safe-to-evict}\n'

maya: perfect. thanks.
